name: The Meridian Isles
summary: An archipelago whose islands drift along invisible magnetic currents.
description: The Meridian Isles circle a blue magnetic rift. During a convergence, stone reefs rise, compasses reverse and navigable channels move hundreds of leagues before dawn.
facts: The archipelago has no permanent geographic center.
Cobalt storms reveal temporary bridges between islands.
Every licensed vessel carries a storm calendar.

name: Astra Harbor
summary: A floating port held in place by twelve chains of magnetized stone.
description: Astra Harbor serves as the archipelago's principal exchange. Its chain towers adjust their pull throughout the day to keep the city beside a stable shipping current.
facts: The Cartographers' Guild certifies every public route.
Chain eleven has weakened since the last convergence.
Unregistered compasses are confiscated at the eastern quay.

name: Cloudstep
summary: A steep island lifted above the sea by a permanent magnetic updraft.
description: Cloudstep drifts above ordinary shipping lanes. Sailors reach it by following sky rays through narrow columns of blue rain.
facts: Metal tools become weightless near the northern cliff.
The oldest storm calendars are carved beneath its observatory.
No ordinary anchor can hold on Cloudstep.

name: The Kelp Vault
summary: A submerged archive woven into a living forest of iron kelp.
description: The Kelp Vault stores navigational records on thin cobalt leaves. Tide Wardens cultivate the archive and release one leaf whenever a lost vessel is found.
facts: The archive can only be entered at slack tide.
Salt golems protect its central catalog.
Orin Reef can read damaged cobalt leaves.

name: Storm Orchard
summary: A terraced island where trees store lightning inside translucent fruit.
description: Storm Orchard farmers guide small cobalt storms between copper trellises. Ripe fruit powers lamps and instruments but bursts if carried across a reversed meridian.
facts: Harvest begins seven days before a convergence.
Tide Wardens forbid copper cutting tools in the upper terraces.
The Cobalt Consortium controls most exports.

name: Cartographers' Guild
summary: A navigators' guild that publishes routes valid for a single magnetic cycle.
description: Guild cartographers combine sky-ray migration, storm calendars and compass readings. Their maps expire after every blue convergence.
facts: A valid guild map bears three changing cobalt marks.
The guild refuses to chart military routes.
Lya Voss leads its experimental survey crew.

name: Tide Wardens
summary: A civic order that protects shared routes, archives and storm shelters.
description: The Tide Wardens maintain public warning beacons and the Kelp Vault. They can close a channel when magnetic conditions make every known route unsafe.
facts: Wardens answer to island councils rather than merchants.
Their green lantern marks a public shelter.
Orin Reef advises their archive keepers.

name: Cobalt Consortium
summary: A merchant alliance seeking exclusive control of storm-powered trade.
description: The Consortium finances fast survey ships and buys expired maps to predict future routes. Its private ledgers hide the cost of failed expeditions.
facts: The Consortium owns seven storm-fruit warehouses.
It offers rewards for unregistered route data.
The Glass Ledger records its concealed losses.

name: Lya Voss
summary: A survey captain who detects route changes through variations in compass song.
description: Lya commands the Cartographers' Guild experimental crew. She trusts measurements over inherited maps and records every failed prediction.
facts: Lya designed the current Meridian Compass housing.
She survived the uncharted thirteenth channel.
She suspects chain eleven was deliberately weakened.

name: Orin Reef
summary: An archivist who reconstructs damaged route records from cobalt leaves.
description: Orin studies changes in the Kelp Vault catalog. He believes the islands follow a long cycle hidden across generations of damaged records.
facts: Orin can distinguish storm damage from deliberate erasure.
He refuses to sell archive copies.
He decoded the first half of the Glass Ledger.

name: Sera Kestrel
summary: A glider pilot who protects Cloudstep's observatory and storm calendars.
description: Sera follows sky-ray schools through dangerous rain columns. Her observations give the first warning of a blue convergence.
facts: Sera never carries iron while flying.
She rescued Lya Voss during the thirteenth-channel survey.
Her glider uses woven storm-fruit fibers.

name: Meridian Compass
summary: A navigation instrument that measures the direction and tone of magnetic currents.
description: The Meridian Compass contains twelve suspended cobalt needles. Their combined tone changes before channels move, allowing a trained navigator to estimate a safe route.
facts: The instrument does not point north.
A cracked needle creates a false low tone.
Lya Voss added a nonmagnetic glass housing.

name: The Glass Ledger
summary: A concealed commercial record etched onto transparent storm glass.
description: The Glass Ledger records lost Consortium ships, secret route purchases and payments to unidentified saboteurs. Its overlapping pages are readable only in a reversed magnetic field.
facts: Orin Reef decoded its first half.
The final page mentions Astra Harbor's chain eleven.
The Consortium claims the ledger is counterfeit.

name: Sky Ray
summary: A broad flying creature that migrates along stable magnetic currents.
description: Sky rays feed on charged mist. Navigators follow their schools because the creatures avoid collapsing currents and violent cobalt storms.
facts: A sky ray's wing edges glow before a route reversal.
Young rays shelter beneath Cloudstep.
Metal noise can scatter a migrating school.

name: Salt Golem
summary: A tidal guardian formed from salt crystals and iron kelp.
description: Salt golems patrol the Kelp Vault without leaving the archive current. They recognize Tide Warden lantern patterns and block anyone carrying cut cobalt leaves.
facts: Fresh water weakens their crystal joints.
They reform after each spring tide.
A green lantern permits supervised passage.

name: Blue Convergence
summary: A rare alignment that reverses the archipelago's magnetic currents.
description: During a blue convergence, islands accelerate toward new routes, dormant reefs rise and every conventional compass reverses. Accurate warnings can prevent entire fleets from entering collapsing channels.
facts: Sky rays migrate upward three days before a convergence.
Storm fruit ripens early during the warning period.
The next convergence is predicted but not yet dated.
